summary: SECOND phase-5 pass (round 2). The first pass wrote a bundle, parked the item at awaiting-uat, then found that FR11 had silently REMOVED the phases' exit write; the item was walked back off the UAT gate on purpose, rounds 04-07 of review and 03-04 of test ran, and this pass re-reconciled everything. Final counts: implement 12 rounds, review 7 (APPROVE, 36 findings - 1 blocker, 6 majors, 23 minors, 6 nits; 28 verified, 8 fixed, 0 open), test 4 (PASS, 3 findings, all verified, open_issues 0). 43 product files (38 modified + 5 new test files), +2115/-174 on tracked product files plus 2743 lines of new tests, 76 new top-level tests. All four gates independently re-run green at this pass, hermetic run included with `claude` absent (12 tested packages); plugin.json and cli/main.go both 0.29.0. FIXED REV-024, the one open finding and explicitly 5's own: the bundle's knowledge table stated the SUPERSEDED entry-only rule at two rows; both now read 'a phase writes its occupancy status at entry AND AGAIN at exit - two writers on purpose, because one of them is an LLM following prose', matching coding-rules.md and non-functional-requirements.md, and the disputed variant count is settled at FOURTEEN (test-strategy.md's heading, the report, and code-review-standards.md #12's cross-reference, which was corrected from 'ten' in this pass). Rewrote all four as-built diagrams (flow/sequence/activity/class) - the sequence and activity views now carry BOTH writers, and the flow and class views carry the m/M legality chain (decision gate -> plan readiness -> accept -> runnable -> cap, only the cap forceable by M) and the single moveChip producer that rounds 04-07 added; layouts.json rebuilt for the after set (4 laid out, 0 skipped) and the before set (2, 0 skipped), before/*.mmd re-copied md5-verified, both manifests validate against charts-manifest.schema.json. Knowledge: test-strategy.md's fourteen variants regrouped so 11-14 are no longer orphaned after the closing summary and the control-pair technique added; code-review-standards.md #12's stale count fixed (#13, which protects the exit write from being flagged as duplication, was already correct); project-knowledge.md's 0.29.0 entry extended with the later rounds and the 7-round process finding. adjustments.md gained the rounds 05-08 section REV-028 asked for and never got. THE REPORT IS HONEST ABOUT WHAT DID NOT WORK: FR11's writer half is a hypothesis that has not paid off (n=3, skipped every live run, phase 4 too); it also caused an unplanned regression by dropping the exit write, making a skipped entry write leave the line stale INDEFINITELY rather than one phase late, which 5 caught and the user reverted; the release claim is scoped to 'the board narrates the present for 2; for 3/4/5 it either narrates the present or says out loud that it cannot'; the cue's meaning is only 'state.md and events.jsonl disagree about the current phase, one half of step 1 did not land' and its silence is not proof of health; and the restored exit write costs a hand-off blink, accepted knowingly. Three shipped-then-caught defects are recorded rather than hidden: a bare `gogo sweep` recommended as a remedy (host-global, would kill another source's live build - still UNCONFIRMED by design, never executed), an ABORTED feature told it had 'already shipped' (aligned to a runnableHint arm cmdGo never reaches), and footer chips promising '[m] go' on cards that bounce. The process is recorded as a finding too: 7 review rounds against a ~3-round bound, with several later rounds fixing defects earlier fixes introduced, including the orchestrator's. Carried forward: FR11's advisory writer, REV-035 (a mid-write state.md can drop a legitimate ship selection - judged the safer direction: degrade to missing, never wrong), REV-036 (uatRound takes the first integer anywhere after 'uat'), a FOURTH orphaned-doc occurrence found at 5 at cli/internal/tui/move.go:192-193 (not fixed - 5 writes only under .gogo/), cross-source sweep owner resolution, bare `gogo sweep` confirmation, and 0.28.0's cross-repo OVER-count which is the opposite direction from this release's UNDER-count. Landed at awaiting-uat; nothing committed, nothing shipped.
